outsiders.name: Min Choi
outsiders.text:
Hollywood is literally bringing AI VFX onto movie sets now.

"Young Washington" director Jon Erwin says his AI team gets footage just 30 SECONDS after cameras stop rolling.

He's using Seedance 2.5 to visualize scenes BEFORE they're even filmed. 🤯

Here's how his workflow is changing filmmaking:

1. Make the movie BEFORE making the movie.

Erwin is using Seedance 2.5 to visualize scripts before production begins.

Instead of making creative decisions based entirely on words on paper, directors can actually see how scenes might look and refine them.

He calls it bringing Pixar's process to live-action filmmaking.

2. AI VFX can happen DURING filming.

Traditionally, major VFX work happens much later in production.

Erwin is changing that.

He wants a generative AI team working like a second camera unit on set.

Real actors are filming while AI artists develop visual effects alongside them.

3. Footage reaches the AI team in just 30 SECONDS.

This part is pretty incredible.

Erwin says his team can access footage 30 seconds after the camera stops recording.

That means they can start creating and testing effects almost immediately.

Imagine seeing different visual possibilities while you're still shooting the scene.

4. They already reworked a movie's VFX in TWO WEEKS.

Erwin says his team reopened a nearly finished film and regenerated much of its visual effects using Seedance 2.0.

They also chose to shoot entirely on location in Ireland rather than use a soundstage.

Real footage + AI-generated effects.

5. AI is learning the actual language of filmmaking.

ALEXA 65. Cooke lenses. f/1.2.

These are the kinds of instructions professional cinematographers use.

Erwin says Seedance 2.5 is increasingly able to interpret these technical filmmaking terms directly.

6. And he doesn't want AI replacing real actors.

This is important.

Erwin believes human performances are fundamental to filmmaking.

He supports protecting intellectual property and says actors should never lose control over their performances through unauthorized digital replicas.

The bigger picture?

Imagine developing your screenplay visually, filming with real actors, and creating VFX alongside production.

Smaller filmmaking teams could potentially create scenes that previously required much bigger budgets and crews.

And Hollywood directors are already experimenting with this workflow.

Watch Jon Erwin's interview below. 👇

outsiders.hook: Thread on director Jon Erwin using Seedance 2.5 on the set of 'Young Washington': AI previs before filming and VFX footage 30 seconds after the cameras stop.
outsiders.video_tip: Post a previs-vs-final split: a Seedance storyboard shot on the left, your finished shot on the right, captioned 'make the movie before the movie'.
outsiders.draft_en:
AI VFX is moving onto real movie sets, and Jon Erwin's "Young Washington" shows how.

The workflow, step by step:

1. Previs first. Seedance 2.5 turns the script into moving pictures before production starts, so choices are made on visuals instead of pages - he compares it to how Pixar works, applied to live action.

2. VFX during the shoot. A generative AI team acts like a second camera unit, building effects next to the real actors instead of months later.

3. Speed. Footage lands with the AI artists 30 SECONDS after the camera cuts, so effects get tested almost instantly.

4. Rework. His crew went back into a film that was almost done and rebuilt a large share of the effects with Seedance 2.0 in TWO WEEKS, and shot on location in Ireland instead of a soundstage.

5. Camera language. Seedance 2.5 increasingly understands cinematographer terms like ALEXA 65, Cooke lenses and f/1.2.

6. Actors stay central. He sees human performance as the core of film, backs IP protection and opposes unauthorized digital replicas.

Small crews could soon pull off scenes that once needed huge budgets, and Hollywood directors are already testing it. His full interview is below.

virals.name: Min Choi
virals.text:
Hollywood is literally bringing AI VFX onto movie sets now.

"Young Washington" director Jon Erwin says his AI team gets footage just 30 SECONDS after cameras stop rolling.

He's using Seedance 2.5 to visualize scenes BEFORE they're even filmed. 🤯

Here's how his workflow is changing filmmaking:

1. Make the movie BEFORE making the movie.

Erwin is using Seedance 2.5 to visualize scripts before production begins.

Instead of making creative decisions based entirely on words on paper, directors can actually see how scenes might look and refine them.

He calls it bringing Pixar's process to live-action filmmaking.

2. AI VFX can happen DURING filming.

Traditionally, major VFX work happens much later in production.

Erwin is changing that.

He wants a generative AI team working like a second camera unit on set.

Real actors are filming while AI artists develop visual effects alongside them.

3. Footage reaches the AI team in just 30 SECONDS.

This part is pretty incredible.

Erwin says his team can access footage 30 seconds after the camera stops recording.

That means they can start creating and testing effects almost immediately.

Imagine seeing different visual possibilities while you're still shooting the scene.

4. They already reworked a movie's VFX in TWO WEEKS.

Erwin says his team reopened a nearly finished film and regenerated much of its visual effects using Seedance 2.0.

They also chose to shoot entirely on location in Ireland rather than use a soundstage.

Real footage + AI-generated effects.

5. AI is learning the actual language of filmmaking.

ALEXA 65. Cooke lenses. f/1.2.

These are the kinds of instructions professional cinematographers use.

Erwin says Seedance 2.5 is increasingly able to interpret these technical filmmaking terms directly.

6. And he doesn't want AI replacing real actors.

This is important.

Erwin believes human performances are fundamental to filmmaking.

He supports protecting intellectual property and says actors should never lose control over their performances through unauthorized digital replicas.

The bigger picture?

Imagine developing your screenplay visually, filming with real actors, and creating VFX alongside production.

Smaller filmmaking teams could potentially create scenes that previously required much bigger budgets and crews.

And Hollywood directors are already experimenting with this workflow.

Watch Jon Erwin's interview below. 👇

virals.video_tip: Post a previs-vs-final split: a Seedance storyboard shot on the left, your finished shot on the right, captioned 'make the movie before the movie'.
virals.draft_en:
AI VFX is moving onto real movie sets, and Jon Erwin's "Young Washington" shows how.

The workflow, step by step:

1. Previs first. Seedance 2.5 turns the script into moving pictures before production starts, so choices are made on visuals instead of pages - he compares it to how Pixar works, applied to live action.

2. VFX during the shoot. A generative AI team acts like a second camera unit, building effects next to the real actors instead of months later.

3. Speed. Footage lands with the AI artists 30 SECONDS after the camera cuts, so effects get tested almost instantly.

4. Rework. His crew went back into a film that was almost done and rebuilt a large share of the effects with Seedance 2.0 in TWO WEEKS, and shot on location in Ireland instead of a soundstage.

5. Camera language. Seedance 2.5 increasingly understands cinematographer terms like ALEXA 65, Cooke lenses and f/1.2.

6. Actors stay central. He sees human performance as the core of film, backs IP protection and opposes unauthorized digital replicas.

Small crews could soon pull off scenes that once needed huge budgets, and Hollywood directors are already testing it. His full interview is below.

x_keywords.method: Read-only x MCP search_posts_all, 2 calls per keyword: last 24 h and previous 24 h (24-48 h ago); lang:en, no retweets/replies, sort=relevancy, up to 25 posts per window. This is a SAMPLE of top-relevance posts, not every post on X. Views = impression_count at fetch time. Rank = sum of sampled 24 h views; 48 h = both windows; trend = 24 h sum / previous 24 h sum (up >=1.3, down <=0.7). Fresh posts are still gaining views, so 'up' is understated. Top-post share > 70% means one viral post carries the keyword.

trend_radar.legend: Trend match 0-100% = 1 - prod(1 - w) over matched 24 h keywords that another author also used in the 48 h window (w: rank 1-10 0.35, 11-25 0.22, 26-40 0.12, curated 0.20). Verdict: >= 50% -> trend; else video/image in the post data -> visual; else >= 100K followers (outsiders without follower data: >= 500K views, estimate) -> author/audience; else coincidence/other. Missing data shows as 'no data'. Heat = sum log10(views) of topic posts (24 h x1, 24-48 h x0.5), scaled to 100. Momentum = log-views last 24 h / previous 24 h. Trend-input-only accounts feed the corpus but are never shown as hits.
